name: Question 19
problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}-t{y}^{′}+10y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y=t({c}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\operatorname{ln}⁡t)+{c}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\operatorname{ln}⁡t)),
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}-t{y}^{′}+10y=0,\,y(1)=2,\,{y}^{′}(1)=-4,\,t>0.
$$
worked_solution:
We find the constants ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial conditions.

- Substituting $y(1)=2$ into the general solution gives

$$
2={c}_{1}.
$$

- To apply the condition ${y}^{′}(1)=-4,$ we first differentiate $y$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & =({c}_{1}+3{c}_{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\operatorname{ln}⁡t)+({c}_{2}-3{c}_{1})\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\operatorname{ln}⁡t).\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute ${y}^{′}(1)=-4$ and ${c}_{1}=2$ into the above to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-4 & =2+3{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{2} & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y(t)=2t(\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\operatorname{ln}⁡t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\operatorname{ln}⁡t)).
$$

Question 19
?

Given that the differential equation t2y″−ty′+10y=0 has the general solution y=t(c1cos⁡(3ln⁡t)+c2sin⁡(3ln⁡t)), solve the initial value problem t2y″−ty′+10y=0,y(1)=2,y′(1)=−4,t>0.

a
y(t)=t(2cos⁡(3ln⁡t)−3sin⁡(3ln⁡t))
b
y(t)=3t(cos⁡(3ln⁡t)−sin⁡(3ln⁡t))
c
y(t)=2t(cos⁡(3ln⁡t)−sin⁡(3ln⁡t))
d
y(t)=2t(cos⁡(3ln⁡t)+sin⁡(3ln⁡t))
e
y(t)=t(3cos⁡(3ln⁡t)−2sin⁡(3ln⁡t))
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We find the constants c1 and c2 using the initial conditions.

  • Substituting y(1)=2 into the general solution gives 2=c1.

  • To apply the condition y′(1)=−4, we first differentiate y to get y′(x)=(c1+3c2)cos⁡(3ln⁡t)+(c2−3c1)sin⁡(3ln⁡t). Then, we substitute y′(1)=−4 and c1=2 into the above to get −4=2+3c2c2=−2.

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is y(t)=2t(cos⁡(3ln⁡t)−sin⁡(3ln⁡t)).
